title: Criteria that Qualify for Intervention by Community Relations Unit and Unit's Effectiveness in Addressing Neighbourly Disputes
what_it_is: Criteria that Qualify for Intervention by Community Relations Unit and Unit's Effectiveness in Addressing Neighbourly Disputes

sections.label: Community Relations Unit pilot outcomes
sections.summary: Asked how many cases the Community Relations Unit resolved or closed since its April 2025 pilot launch and the Ministry's assessment of its effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development since the pilot launch of the Community Relations Unit (CRU) in April 2025 (a) how many cases have been resolved or closed by the CRU; and (b) what is the Ministry’s assessment of the effectiveness of the CRU in addressing severe neighbour disputes involving noise and hoarding.

sections.label: Tampines CRU noise sensor cases
sections.summary: In five Tampines cases CRU investigated since April, noise sensors were not required because noisemakers gave formal statements or the source was clear.

sentences.text: In the five cases in the pilot town of Tampines that CRU has investigated since April this year, noise sensors were not required because either the noisemakers gave formal statements that confirmed they were the source of noise, or the source of noise was clear and unambiguous.

sections.label: CRU mental health-related cases
sections.summary: Of three mental health-related cases CRU is dealing with, it facilitated inpatient admission and treatment for one and more consistent community follow-up for two.

sentences.text: Of the three mental health-related cases CRU is dealing with, it has facilitated inpatient admission and treatment for one, and more consistent follow-up with the community for the other two.

sections.label: HDB floor slab thickness increase
sections.summary: For new Build-To-Order developments since February 2023, HDB has increased floor slab thickness to 200 millimetres.

sentences.text: For new Build-To-Order (BTO) developments since February 2023, HDB has increased the thickness of floor slabs to 200 millimetres.

sections.label: HDB neighbour noise feedback volume
sections.summary: The average monthly volume of neighbour noise feedback in HDB estates across Singapore over the past five years has held steady at about 2,500.

sentences.text: Overall, the average monthly volume of neighbour noise feedback in HDB estates, across Singapore, over the past five years has held steady at about 2,500.

sections.label: CDRT enforcement and CRU thresholds
sections.summary: A supplementary question raised perceptions that CDRT are toothless, noted CRU's 15 staff and five severe cases in six months, and asked about escalation thresholds and published criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Supplementary question three, there is widespread perception that the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals (CDRT) are quite toothless because, even if you get an injunction, getting an enforcement order seems to be quite difficult.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For MND, the first supplementary question, so, the CRU has 15 staff members, has had five severe cases in six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: That means less than one case per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And yet, there are about 2,500 noise cases per month, so generally, using the Tampines electors as a proxy for the number of cases, there should have been about 150 cases for Tampines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My question is, what are the thresholds preventing CRU escalation and will MND publish the criteria so that residents and frontline officers know when a case is deemed severe?

sections.label: Special direction breach penalties
sections.summary: Breaching a special direction can lead to prosecution and conviction, and CDRT or HDB can evict a person from his house.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The legislative framework allows for a person who breaches a special direction to be prosecuted and be convicted, and that must mean that there is some tooth to the action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: And may I also add that, under the enhanced powers, the CDRT or the HDB has even the powers to evict a person from his house.

sections.label: Tampines pilot expansion study
sections.summary: The six-month Tampines pilot is resource intensive and being studied carefully, with severe cases continuing and expansion where appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Can I ask and can I also request for Members to understand this: that this is a pilot, we have done this for six months in Tampines and it is resource intensive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We are now only six months into this one-year pilot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And we will continue to take on severe cases in Tampines that are being floated to, or raised or triaged by the agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We are studying this pilot very carefully, sizing it very carefully and where appropriate, we will expand this pilot.

sections.label: Resourcing and extending beyond Tampines
sections.summary: Taken together, they can look at how best to resource this and extend it beyond Tampines when appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Taken together, we are able to then look at how best to resource this and then extend it to beyond Tampines, when it is appropriate.

sections.label: CRU cases and expansion timing
sections.summary: Five CRU cases are described, including one MD, and the Ministry's decision on expanding CRU to other towns is asked about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Out of the five cases that CRU has taken, how many of those cases are considered resolved and how long did they take?

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second question, when can we expect the Ministry to decide if the CRU can be expanded to other towns – will it be after the one-year period pilot?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I had mentioned earlier on, going into the details of the cases, there are five cases, I mentioned that of the three cases that CRU is dealing with is to facilitate inpatient admission and treatment for one, and more consistent follow-up in community for the other two.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Murali had mentioned that the CRU had issued an MD for one, and then, I also mentioned in my main reply, please refer to that, that the one case involving the deliberate use of noise to disturb neighbours and not related to mental health, has abated after joint intervention by CRU, Police and Town Council.

sections.label: Judiciary assisting CDRT applicants
sections.summary: On assisting applicants in the CDRT process, the Judiciary has leaned forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Insofar as the point about assisting applicants in the CDRT process, certainly the Judiciary has leaned forward.

sections.label: Training grassroots leaders for mediation
sections.summary: They are happy to lean forward to train suitable grassroots leaders for mediation training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As to the supplementary questions on supporting the grassroots leaders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Certainly, we are happy to lean forward to train suitable grassroots leaders for mediation training.

sections.label: Calling Police via 999
sections.summary: Anyone who feels threatened should first call the Police via 999.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: If anyone feels threatened, then the first thing to do is to call the Police via 999.

sections.label: Special powers and CRU standby officers
sections.summary: The Act as amended last year gives special legal powers, and the speaker clarifies his earlier statement about CRU standby officers after office hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Because under the Act as we amended last year, they do have actually special powers, legal powers anyway, under the provisions of the Bill that we passed last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The other question is that he quoted my speech earlier about the fact that, and of course I do recognise that the work is not going to be easy, but I did say, perhaps erroneously last year that the CRU had standby officers after office hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim is right on that second point, so clarified.

sections.label: Service of CDRT order
sections.summary: The issue of service of the CDRT order is a judicial matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The issue of service of the CDRT order is really a judicial matter.

sections.label: Enforcement figures and mediation non-attendance
sections.summary: The speaker lacks enforcement figures off-hand, notes two thirds of disputes relate to noise, and about 50% asked to go for voluntary mediation do not do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As to the steps to be taken to enforce, or rather the figures for enforcement, my apologies, I do not have the figures off-hand, but if the hon Member would like to file a Parliamentary Question, I can answer that specifically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Picking on some of the points that Senior Minister of State made, I understand that two thirds of the disputes relate to noise related matters and about 50% of people who are asked to go for voluntary mediation, do not do so.

sections.label: CRU pilot referral rate
sections.summary: The question asks whether five cases in six months is the expected referral rate for a typical HDB town.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given that the CRU pilot has taken on only five cases in the six months since it started, is this the rate of referrals that can be expected for a typical HDB town?

sections.label: Powers vested in public officers
sections.summary: The speaker explains that these powers are to be vested in public officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As I have explained in my speech, these powers are to be vested in public officers.

sections.label: Tampines pilot private estates extension
sections.summary: The plan starts with Tampines as a pilot and will extend to other towns, including private estates, and HDB will consider compulsory acquisition of flats by severe nuisance makers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I just want to seek clarification, whether this plan also includes private estates like condominiums and private apartments, because I am not just concerned about my HDB residents, I am also concerned about my private estate residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We are focused on Tampines town now as a pilot and after getting all of the feedback and all of the learnings from it, the plan is to extend it to other towns, including where there are private estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I understand HDB will consider compulsory acquisition of flats by severe and recalcitrant nuisance makers.

sections.label: Mandatory logging and soundproofing requests
sections.summary: The member asks whether a mandatory logging and tracking system will be implemented and whether subsidised soundproofing will be considered under future Home Improvement Programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: To ensure we address the structural root issue, can the Minister of State clarify whether they will commit to immediately implementing a mandatory logging and tracking system, and with which agency, to monitor all dispute cases that are reported to involve threats of physical violence in order to identify and flag these recalcitrant offenders, or even consider providing equipment like industrial grade sound monitoring for rental?

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: My second question is, given the limited scope for major infrastructure changes in existing flats, will the Ministry consider exploring subsidised soundproofing improvements or technology, as a specific upgrade option under future Home Improvement Programmes for blocks that have high persistent record of noise related disputes?

sections.label: Special Directions and Exclusion Orders
sections.summary: In the past five years, 24 Special Directions and two Exclusion Orders were issued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In the past five years, there are 24 Special Directions issued and two Exclusion Orders issued.

sections.label: Tampines monthly neighbour noise feedback
sections.summary: Since April 2025, there has been about 160 neighbour noise feedback per month in Tampines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Since April 2025, there has been about 160 neighbour noise feedback per month in Tampines.
